Business.purpose_definition: the evaluation, discussion, negotiation, assessment, and exploration of a potential business relationship, commercial arrangement, transaction, collaboration, strategic opportunity, or other business opportunity between the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss a potential business relationship, commercial arrangement, transaction, collaboration, or other business opportunity;

WHEREAS, in connection with such discussions, either Party may disclose certain confidential, proprietary, technical, commercial, financial, operational, strategic, or business information to the other Party;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Business Opportunity: "Business Opportunity" means any actual, proposed, contemplated, or potential transaction, project, investment, acquisition, merger, joint venture, strategic alliance, partnership, procurement opportunity, service engagement, licensing arrangement, distribution arrangement, commercial relationship, customer engagement, supplier relationship, acquisition opportunity, or other opportunity discussed, evaluated, negotiated, or pursued by the Parties in connection with the Purpose.
additional_definitions.Commercial Information: "Commercial Information" means any information relating to the commercial, business, operational, strategic, marketing, sales, procurement, or financial activities of a Party, including pricing information, quotations, bids, tenders, commercial proposals, business plans, market strategies, customer acquisition strategies, sales forecasts, profit margins, revenue models, procurement plans, contractual arrangements, and other commercially sensitive information.
additional_definitions.Business Relationship: "Business Relationship" means any existing, proposed, prospective, or contemplated commercial relationship, transaction, engagement, collaboration, partnership, service arrangement, supply arrangement, licensing arrangement, procurement arrangement, investment relationship, or other business interaction between the Parties or involving a Party and a third party.
additional_definitions.Strategic Information: "Strategic Information" means any information relating to the long-term objectives, growth plans, expansion plans, investment strategies, business initiatives, organizational strategies, restructuring plans, acquisition plans, partnership strategies, or other strategic decisions of a Party.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) business plans, strategic plans, growth plans, expansion plans, and market entry strategies;
(b) financial information, budgets, forecasts, financial models, pricing structures, profit margins, cost data, revenue projections, investment plans, and funding strategies;
(c) customer information, customer lists, customer requirements, purchasing history, customer contracts, customer communications, and customer relationship information;

(d) supplier, vendor, distributor, contractor, consultant, advisor, and service provider information, including commercial arrangements, procurement information, pricing structures, and contractual terms;
(e) commercial proposals, quotations, bids, tenders, requests for proposals, requests for quotations, procurement documents, and related negotiations;
(f) product information, service information, product roadmaps, development plans, commercialization strategies, product specifications, and business methodologies;
(g) operational processes, internal procedures, workflows, policies, management reports, business processes, and operational information;
(h) marketing plans, advertising strategies, sales strategies, market research, market intelligence, and competitive analyses;
(i) intellectual property information, proprietary methodologies, trade secrets, know-how, inventions, concepts, and innovations; and
(j) any other proprietary, strategic, commercial, financial, operational, or business information disclosed in connection with the Purpose.
introduced_contacts: Generate the final NDA using the Master NDA structure.

Strategic Partnership.purpose_definition: the evaluation, discussion, negotiation, structuring, development, establishment, and implementation of a potential strategic partnership, alliance, collaboration, consortium, or long-term commercial relationship between the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss a potential strategic partnership, alliance, collaboration, consortium, or other long-term commercial relationship;
WHEREAS, in connection with such discussions, the Parties may exchange confidential commercial, operational, financial, technical, strategic, and proprietary information;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Strategic Partnership: "Strategic Partnership" means any proposed collaboration, alliance, consortium, joint initiative, commercial arrangement, business relationship, or cooperative undertaking between the Parties intended to achieve mutually beneficial commercial, operational, financial, technological, or strategic objectives.
additional_definitions.Partnership Opportunity: "Partnership Opportunity" means any actual, proposed, contemplated, or potential project, transaction, business relationship, investment opportunity, commercial initiative, market opportunity, or strategic undertaking arising from or relating to the proposed Strategic Partnership.
additional_definitions.Strategic Information: "Strategic Information" means information relating to the business objectives, growth strategies, expansion plans, market positioning, competitive strategies, partnership initiatives, investment plans, organizational development plans, and long-term strategic goals of a Party.
additional_definitions.Collaboration Information: "Collaboration Information" means information relating to proposed cooperation frameworks, governance structures, operational models, commercial arrangements, business plans, project execution strategies, or other collaborative activities contemplated by the Parties.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) strategic partnership proposals, collaboration frameworks, consortium structures, and alliance models;
(b) business development plans, market expansion plans, market entry strategies, and growth initiatives;
(c) revenue-sharing structures, commercial arrangements, pricing strategies, and partnership economics;
(d) governance frameworks, decision-making structures, management arrangements, and organizational models;
(e) operational plans, project execution plans, resource allocation plans, and implementation strategies;
(f) customer acquisition strategies, market intelligence, competitive analyses, and business development opportunities;
(g) investment plans, funding strategies, financial projections, budgets, and commercial forecasts;
(h) proposed roles and responsibilities of the Parties within the contemplated Strategic Partnership;
(i) proprietary methodologies, know-how, business processes, trade secrets, and intellectual property relevant to the contemplated collaboration; and
(j) any other information relating to the establishment, negotiation, implementation, operation, or management of a proposed Strategic Partnership.

Joint Venture.purpose_definition: the evaluation, discussion, negotiation, structuring, formation, financing, implementation, operation, management, and potential establishment of a joint venture, consortium, strategic alliance, special purpose vehicle, partnership, or other collaborative business arrangement between the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss a potential joint venture, consortium, special purpose vehicle, strategic alliance, partnership, or other collaborative business arrangement;
WHEREAS, in connection with such discussions, the Parties may disclose and exchange confidential commercial, financial, technical, operational, legal, strategic, and proprietary information;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Joint Venture: "Joint Venture" means the proposed collaboration, partnership, consortium, special purpose vehicle, contractual alliance, incorporated entity, unincorporated arrangement, or other business undertaking contemplated by the Parties pursuant to the Purpose.
additional_definitions.JV Opportunity: "JV Opportunity" means any actual, proposed, contemplated, or potential project, transaction, investment, commercial arrangement, procurement opportunity, development opportunity, customer engagement, business initiative, or undertaking evaluated in connection with the proposed Joint Venture.
additional_definitions.SPV: "SPV" or "Special Purpose Vehicle" means any company, limited liability partnership, partnership, trust, joint venture entity, project vehicle, or other legal entity that may be established, acquired, or utilized in connection with the Joint Venture.
additional_definitions.JV Information: "JV Information" means information relating to the proposed Joint Venture, including ownership structures, governance frameworks, capital contribution arrangements, management structures, operational arrangements, funding mechanisms, business plans, financial models, and transaction documents.
additional_definitions.Capital Contribution: "Capital Contribution" means any monetary contribution, equity investment, debt funding, asset transfer, intellectual property contribution, service contribution, technology contribution, resource commitment, or other form of contribution proposed to be made by a Party in connection with the Joint Venture.
additional_definitions.Governance Framework: "Governance Framework" means the proposed management, decision-making, oversight, voting, approval, reporting, control, compliance, and organizational structure applicable to the Joint Venture.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) joint venture proposals, consortium structures, partnership models, collaboration frameworks, and special purpose vehicle structures;
(b) ownership structures, equity participation arrangements, shareholding proposals, voting rights, and governance frameworks;
(c) capital contribution plans, funding strategies, investment structures, financing arrangements, and capital allocation models;
(d) management structures, board composition proposals, reserved matters, approval mechanisms, reporting structures, and operational frameworks;
(e) business plans, financial models, revenue projections, cash flow forecasts, budgets, valuations, and investment analyses;
(f) project opportunities, acquisition opportunities, development opportunities, procurement opportunities, and strategic initiatives evaluated through the proposed Joint Venture;
(g) profit-sharing arrangements, loss-sharing arrangements, dividend policies, distribution mechanisms, and commercial allocation structures;
(h) transaction structures, draft term sheets, draft shareholders' agreements, draft joint venture agreements, investment memoranda, and transaction documents;
(i) exit mechanisms, buy-out arrangements, transfer restrictions, deadlock resolution mechanisms, dissolution plans, and restructuring strategies;
(j) intellectual property contributions, technology sharing arrangements, know-how transfers, proprietary methodologies, and trade secrets proposed to be utilized within the Joint Venture; and

(k) any other commercial, financial, operational, strategic, legal, technical, or proprietary information relating to the evaluation, formation, operation, financing, governance, or management of the proposed Joint Venture.

Investment.purpose_definition: the evaluation, discussion, negotiation, structuring, assessment, and potential consummation of an investment, acquisition of securities, equity participation, strategic investment, capital infusion, financing transaction, or other investment opportunity involving one or more of the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss a potential investment transaction, strategic investment, financing arrangement, capital raise, acquisition of securities, or other investment opportunity;
WHEREAS, in connection with such discussions, the Parties may disclose and exchange confidential commercial, financial, operational, strategic, technical, legal, and proprietary information;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Investment Opportunity: "Investment Opportunity" means any actual, proposed, contemplated, or potential investment transaction, financing transaction, acquisition of securities, capital raise, strategic investment, debt investment, equity investment, convertible instrument investment, or other financial opportunity evaluated in connection with the Purpose.
additional_definitions.Investor Information: "Investor Information" means information relating to an investor's investment strategy, portfolio, investment criteria, return expectations, funding capacity, investment structure preferences, risk parameters, due diligence findings, and investment decision-making processes.
additional_definitions.Funding Information: "Funding Information" means information relating to capital requirements, fundraising strategies, funding structures, financing arrangements, investor outreach activities, use of proceeds, and proposed financing transactions.
additional_definitions.Financial Information: "Financial Information" means financial statements, management accounts, forecasts, budgets, financial models, valuation reports, revenue projections, capital expenditure plans, working capital information, cash flow projections, and other financial data.
additional_definitions.Investment Structure: "Investment Structure" means any proposed share subscription, share purchase, asset acquisition, convertible instrument, debt financing, hybrid financing, partnership structure, or other investment arrangement contemplated by the Parties.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) business plans, growth strategies, investment proposals, funding plans, and capital raising strategies;
(b) financial statements, management accounts, audit reports, budgets, forecasts, financial models, valuations, and financial projections;
(c) capitalization tables, shareholding structures, ownership information, equity allocation plans, and proposed investment structures;
(d) investor presentations, information memoranda, pitch decks, teasers, investment summaries, and transaction documents;
(e) funding requirements, use of proceeds, deployment strategies, expansion plans, acquisition plans, and investment objectives;
(f) due diligence reports, legal reviews, financial reviews, tax reviews, compliance assessments, and risk analyses;
(g) transaction terms, valuation methodologies, pricing assumptions, commercial negotiations, and investment conditions;
(h) intellectual property portfolios, proprietary technologies, trade secrets, business methodologies, and competitive advantages relevant to the investment opportunity;
(i) customer information, supplier information, strategic partnerships, key commercial arrangements, and operational data relevant to the investment decision; and
(j) any other commercial, financial, strategic, legal, technical, operational, or proprietary information disclosed in connection with the evaluation of the Investment Opportunity.

Fundraising.purpose_definition: the evaluation, discussion, negotiation, structuring, marketing, and potential consummation of a fundraising transaction, capital raise, financing round, debt financing, equity financing, strategic funding arrangement, or other capital raising activity involving one or more of the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss a potential fundraising transaction, financing arrangement, capital raise, investment round, or other funding opportunity;
WHEREAS, in connection with such discussions, the Parties may disclose and exchange confidential commercial, financial, operational, strategic, technical, legal, and proprietary information;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Fundraising Transaction: "Fundraising Transaction" means any actual, proposed, contemplated, or potential capital raising activity, equity financing, debt financing, convertible financing, bridge financing, private placement, rights issue, strategic funding arrangement, or other financing transaction evaluated in connection with the Purpose.
additional_definitions.Fundraising Information: "Fundraising Information" means information relating to funding requirements, capital raising plans, investor outreach strategies, financing structures, proposed use of proceeds, funding milestones, transaction terms, and fundraising objectives.
additional_definitions.Investor Materials: "Investor Materials" means pitch decks, information memoranda, teasers, business presentations, investor presentations, executive summaries, business plans, financial models, valuation reports, and other materials prepared for prospective investors.
additional_definitions.Financing Structure: "Financing Structure" means any proposed equity investment, debt financing, convertible instrument, hybrid financing, revenue-based financing, strategic investment, venture financing, private equity investment, or other funding arrangement.
additional_definitions.Use of Proceeds: "Use of Proceeds" means the proposed allocation, deployment, expenditure, investment, or utilization of funds raised through the contemplated Fundraising Transaction.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) fundraising strategies, capital raising plans, financing roadmaps, investor outreach plans, and funding objectives;
(b) investor presentations, pitch decks, teasers, information memoranda, executive summaries, business plans, and marketing materials prepared for investors;
(c) financial statements, budgets, financial forecasts, valuation reports, financial models, cash flow projections, and revenue forecasts;
(d) capitalization tables, ownership structures, shareholding information, option pools, dilution analyses, and proposed equity allocations;
(e) proposed financing structures, investment terms, valuation methodologies, pricing assumptions, term sheets, and transaction documents;
(f) investor communications, investor feedback, fundraising negotiations, investment discussions, and transaction-related correspondence;
(g) business strategies, expansion plans, acquisition plans, product development plans, market penetration strategies, and growth initiatives;
(h) customer information, supplier information, strategic partnerships, key commercial contracts, and operational information relevant to the fundraising process;
(i) due diligence materials, legal reviews, compliance reviews, tax reviews, financial reviews, and risk assessments; and
(j) any other commercial, financial, operational, strategic, legal, technical, or proprietary information disclosed in connection with the contemplated Fundraising Transaction.

Vendor Evaluation.purpose_definition: the evaluation, assessment, selection, qualification, engagement, onboarding, management, or potential appointment of a vendor, contractor, consultant, supplier, service provider, technology provider, or other commercial counterparty by one or more of the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss a potential vendor relationship, procurement opportunity, supply arrangement, service engagement, or commercial relationship;

WHEREAS, in connection with such evaluation and discussions, the Parties may disclose and exchange confidential commercial, financial, operational, technical, legal, procurement-related, and proprietary information;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Vendor: "Vendor" means any supplier, contractor, consultant, service provider, technology provider, distributor, reseller, manufacturer, subcontractor, or other commercial counterparty being evaluated, engaged, appointed, or considered by a Party.
additional_definitions.Vendor Information: "Vendor Information" means information relating to a Vendor's business operations, financial standing, technical capabilities, products, services, personnel, resources, pricing, contractual arrangements, qualifications, certifications, compliance status, and performance history.
additional_definitions.Procurement Information: "Procurement Information" means information relating to procurement strategies, sourcing activities, requests for proposals, requests for quotations, tender processes, bid evaluations, commercial negotiations, procurement plans, purchasing requirements, and supplier selection criteria.
additional_definitions.Vendor Proposal: "Vendor Proposal" means any quotation, proposal, bid, tender submission, response to a request for proposal, response to a request for quotation, capability statement, commercial offer, technical submission, pricing proposal, or similar document submitted or exchanged in connection with the Purpose.
additional_definitions.Evaluation Criteria: "Evaluation Criteria" means the commercial, financial, technical, operational, legal, compliance, quality, performance, sustainability, or other standards used by a Party to assess, compare, qualify, or select a Vendor.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) procurement plans, sourcing strategies, purchasing requirements, procurement forecasts, and procurement budgets;
(b) requests for proposals (RFPs), requests for quotations (RFQs), tender documents, bid specifications, procurement guidelines, and evaluation methodologies;
(c) quotations, pricing proposals, commercial offers, bid submissions, tender responses, pricing structures, discounts, rebates, and commercial negotiations;
(d) technical specifications, statements of work, service descriptions, product specifications, quality standards, acceptance criteria, and implementation requirements;
(e) vendor assessments, qualification reports, evaluation reports, audit findings, performance reviews, compliance assessments, and due diligence reports;
(f) customer requirements, operational requirements, service requirements, project requirements, procurement strategies, and sourcing decisions;
(g) contractual terms, draft agreements, service level requirements, warranty commitments, indemnity structures, and risk allocation mechanisms;
(h) information relating to suppliers, subcontractors, manufacturers, distributors, channel partners, and other commercial counterparties;
(i) business plans, financial information, forecasts, budgets, commercial strategies, and operational information relevant to the vendor evaluation process; and

(j) any other commercial, financial, operational, technical, procurement-related, legal, compliance, or proprietary information disclosed in connection with the evaluation, selection, onboarding, appointment, or management of a Vendor.

Supplier Evaluation.purpose_definition: the evaluation, assessment, qualification, selection, onboarding, engagement, management, or potential appointment of a supplier, manufacturer, distributor, procurement partner, logistics provider, or other supply chain participant by one or more of the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss a potential supplier relationship, procurement arrangement, sourcing opportunity, manufacturing arrangement, distribution arrangement, logistics engagement, or other supply chain relationship;

WHEREAS, in connection with such evaluation and discussions, the Parties may disclose and exchange confidential commercial, financial, operational, technical, procurement-related, supply chain, and proprietary information;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Supplier: "Supplier" means any manufacturer, producer, wholesaler, distributor, trader, importer, exporter, logistics provider, procurement partner, inventory provider, raw material provider, component supplier, equipment supplier, or other entity supplying goods, materials, products, components, equipment, or related services.
additional_definitions.Supplier Information: "Supplier Information" means information relating to a Supplier's production capabilities, manufacturing processes, sourcing arrangements, quality standards, certifications, logistics capabilities, inventory levels, pricing structures, supply capacity, delivery performance, compliance status, and operational capabilities.
additional_definitions.Supply Chain Information: "Supply Chain Information" means information relating to sourcing strategies, procurement activities, manufacturing operations, inventory management, logistics operations, warehousing activities, distribution arrangements, transportation systems, supply planning, and supply chain risk management.
additional_definitions.Sourcing Information: "Sourcing Information" means information relating to supplier identification, procurement planning, sourcing strategies, supplier qualification processes, tender processes, bid evaluations, supplier negotiations, and supplier selection methodologies.
additional_definitions.Supply Arrangement: "Supply Arrangement" means any proposed procurement relationship, supply agreement, framework arrangement, manufacturing arrangement, distribution arrangement, inventory arrangement, logistics arrangement, or sourcing relationship contemplated by the Parties.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) sourcing strategies, procurement plans, supply forecasts, inventory forecasts, demand forecasts, and purchasing requirements;
(b) supplier lists, approved supplier databases, procurement records, sourcing analyses, and supplier qualification reports;
(c) manufacturing processes, production capabilities, capacity utilization reports, production schedules, and operational capabilities;
(d) logistics information, transportation arrangements, warehousing arrangements, inventory management systems, distribution networks, and delivery schedules;
(e) pricing structures, quotations, procurement budgets, sourcing costs, supplier negotiations, rebate structures, and commercial terms;
(f) quality standards, inspection procedures, testing methodologies, audit reports, certifications, compliance reviews, and quality assurance systems;
(g) technical specifications, product requirements, material specifications, component specifications, packaging requirements, and delivery standards;
(h) supply chain risk assessments, contingency plans, business continuity plans, supplier dependency analyses, and supply security strategies;
(i) contractual arrangements, framework agreements, purchase commitments, volume commitments, service level requirements, and procurement policies; and

(j) any other commercial, operational, technical, financial, logistics-related, procurement-related, manufacturing-related, supply chain-related, or proprietary information disclosed in connection with the evaluation, qualification, onboarding, appointment, or management of a Supplier.

Technology Sharing.purpose_definition: the evaluation, discussion, review, demonstration, assessment, transfer, licensing, integration, development, commercialization, or potential collaboration relating to technology, software, systems, intellectual property, technical know-how, inventions, products, services, or related technological solutions between the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss certain technologies, software, systems, intellectual property, technical know-how, inventions, products, services, or related technological solutions;

WHEREAS, in connection with such discussions, demonstrations, evaluations, or collaborations, the Parties may disclose and exchange confidential technical, commercial, financial, operational, proprietary, and intellectual property information;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Technology: "Technology" means any software, hardware, firmware, system, process, methodology, algorithm, database, platform, application, tool, model, design, invention, technical solution, technical know-how, trade secret, or other technological asset or capability.
additional_definitions.Technical Information: "Technical Information" means any technical, scientific, engineering, operational, design, development, testing, implementation, deployment, maintenance, support, or performance-related information relating to Technology.
additional_definitions.Intellectual Property: "Intellectual Property" means patents, patent applications, copyrights, trademarks, service marks, trade names, trade secrets, know-how, industrial designs, database rights, domain names, proprietary rights, and all other intellectual property rights recognized under Applicable Law.
additional_definitions.Proprietary Technology: "Proprietary Technology" means any Technology owned, controlled, developed, licensed, or otherwise possessed by a Party that is not publicly available and derives actual or potential commercial value from its confidentiality.
additional_definitions.Source Materials: "Source Materials" means source code, object code, technical documentation, design specifications, development materials, engineering documents, architectural diagrams, models, schematics, databases, and related materials associated with Technology.
additional_definitions.Technical Documentation: means the human-readable form of software, including programming instructions, scripts, comments, libraries, modules, interfaces, and related development materials used to create, modify, maintain, compile, or execute software.
additional_definitions.Application Programming Interface (API): "API" or "Application Programming Interface" means any interface, protocol, specification, documentation, or related technology that enables communication, integration, interoperability, or data exchange between software systems, applications, platforms, or services.
additional_definitions.Know-How: "Know-How" means technical knowledge, expertise, experience, methodologies, processes, techniques, practices, skills, procedures, and proprietary information that may not be protected by formal intellectual property rights but possesses actual or potential commercial value.
additional_definitions.Research and Development Information: "Research and Development Information" or "R&D Information" means research, development, testing, experimentation, validation, innovation, engineering, scientific, technical, and product development information generated, utilized, or evaluated in connection with research and development activities.
additional_definitions.Licensed Technology: "Licensed Technology" means any Technology that is licensed, proposed to be licensed, sublicensed, evaluated for licensing, transferred, commercialized, or otherwise made available by one Party to the other Party.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) software applications, software architecture, source code, object code, databases, APIs, software development kits (SDKs), libraries, and software documentation;
(b) algorithms, formulas, methodologies, technical models, engineering processes, workflows, designs, specifications, and technical solutions;
(c) inventions, innovations, discoveries, research results, technical concepts, prototypes, proof-of-concepts, and product development information;
(d) technical drawings, schematics, architecture diagrams, system configurations, network designs, deployment models, and infrastructure information;
(e) technical documentation, user manuals, operating procedures, engineering documents, testing reports, validation reports, and implementation materials;
(f) research and development information, product roadmaps, development plans, release schedules, upgrade plans, and technology strategies;
(g) intellectual property portfolios, patent strategies, patent applications, copyright materials, trade secrets, know-how, and proprietary methodologies;
(h) technical performance data, benchmark results, security assessments, vulnerability reports, system logs, analytics, monitoring information, and technical audit reports;
(i) licensing arrangements, technology transfer arrangements, commercialization plans, technology partnerships, and technical collaboration frameworks; and

(j) any other technical, scientific, engineering, software-related, intellectual property-related, operational, commercial, financial, or proprietary information disclosed in connection with the Purpose.

(k) source code repositories, development environments, build systems, deployment pipelines, continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) processes, version control systems, and software engineering workflows;
(l) APIs, API documentation, integration specifications, interface requirements, interoperability frameworks, communication protocols, and data exchange mechanisms;

(m) artificial intelligence models, machine learning models, training methodologies, training datasets, inference methodologies, model architectures, model weights, model outputs, and model performance information;

(n) cybersecurity controls, security architecture, penetration testing reports, vulnerability assessments, security procedures, incident response plans, disaster recovery plans, and security monitoring information;
(o) cloud architecture, hosting arrangements, infrastructure configurations, virtualization environments, containerization systems, orchestration platforms, and system administration information; and
(p) research results, technical experiments, feasibility studies, proof-of-concepts, prototypes, validation reports, product testing information, and technical evaluation materials.

Commercial Due Diligence.purpose_definition: the evaluation, review, assessment, verification, investigation, analysis, and conduct of commercial due diligence in connection with a proposed transaction, investment, acquisition, financing, partnership, strategic relationship, procurement arrangement, or other business opportunity.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and conduct commercial due diligence in relation to a proposed transaction, investment, partnership, acquisition, financing arrangement, commercial opportunity, or business relationship;

WHEREAS, in connection with such due diligence activities, the Parties may disclose and exchange confidential commercial, financial, operational, technical, strategic, legal, compliance, and proprietary information;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Due Diligence Information: "Due Diligence Information" means any information, document, material, report, record, analysis, presentation, data room content, correspondence, or other information disclosed, reviewed, exchanged, or generated in connection with the conduct of due diligence.
additional_definitions.Data Room: "Data Room" means any physical or virtual repository, platform, portal, storage environment, electronic system, or information-sharing mechanism used to provide access to Due Diligence Information.
additional_definitions.Target Business: "Target Business" means the business, undertaking, division, project, operation, assets, entity, investment opportunity, commercial opportunity, or transaction subject to the due diligence review.
additional_definitions.Evaluation Materials: "Evaluation Materials" means all analyses, compilations, notes, summaries, reports, memoranda, studies, models, presentations, assessments, and other materials prepared by or on behalf of a Party that contain, reflect, are based upon, or otherwise incorporate Due Diligence Information.
additional_definitions.Commercial Due Diligence: "Commercial Due Diligence" means the review, verification, investigation, assessment, and evaluation of the commercial, operational, strategic, market, customer, supplier, competitive, and business aspects of the Target Business.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) corporate records, organizational information, ownership information, group structures, and business profiles;
(b) customer information, customer contracts, customer concentration analyses, customer retention information, customer acquisition strategies, and customer performance data;
(c) supplier information, procurement information, vendor contracts, sourcing arrangements, supply chain information, and procurement strategies;
(d) business plans, strategic plans, expansion plans, growth initiatives, market entry strategies, and business development initiatives;
(e) financial statements, management accounts, budgets, forecasts, revenue reports, profitability analyses, and financial models;
(f) operational information, business processes, workflows, operational reports, operational performance metrics, and management information;
(g) market studies, market intelligence, industry reports, competitive analyses, benchmarking studies, and commercial assessments;
(h) pricing information, commercial terms, contract structures, commercial arrangements, procurement arrangements, and negotiation materials;
(i) regulatory information, compliance information, licenses, permits, certifications, internal policies, and compliance assessments;
(j) risk assessments, audit reports, internal reviews, business continuity plans, contingency plans, and operational assessments;
(k) intellectual property information, proprietary methodologies, trade secrets, know-how, technology assets, and commercialization information;
(l) information contained within any Data Room, virtual data room, management presentation, due diligence report, information memorandum, or transaction document; and

(m) any other commercial, operational, financial, strategic, technical, compliance-related, legal, regulatory, or proprietary information disclosed in connection with the Commercial Due Diligence process.

M&a Due Diligence.purpose_definition: the evaluation, review, investigation, assessment, structuring, negotiation, and potential consummation of a merger, acquisition, share purchase, asset purchase, business combination, restructuring transaction, investment transaction, or other strategic corporate transaction involving one or more of the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss a potential merger, acquisition, business combination, investment transaction, restructuring transaction, share purchase, asset purchase, or other strategic corporate transaction;

WHEREAS, in connection with such evaluation, discussions, negotiations, and due diligence activities, the Parties may disclose and exchange confidential commercial, financial, operational, technical, legal, tax, compliance, strategic, and proprietary information;
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to establish the terms and conditions governing the disclosure, protection, use, and handling of such Confidential Information.

additional_definitions.Transaction: "Transaction" means the proposed merger, acquisition, share purchase, asset purchase, business combination, restructuring, investment transaction, strategic investment, joint acquisition, corporate reorganization, or other transaction contemplated by the Parties.
additional_definitions.Target Company: "Target Company" means the company, business, undertaking, project, division, subsidiary, affiliate, assets, securities, or operations that are the subject of the proposed Transaction.
additional_definitions.Transaction Information: "Transaction Information" means information relating to the Transaction, including transaction structures, valuation analyses, pricing assumptions, negotiation positions, transaction documents, due diligence findings, and proposed transaction terms.
additional_definitions.Due Diligence Information: "Due Diligence Information" means all information, documents, records, reports, analyses, presentations, correspondence, data room content, and other materials disclosed, reviewed, exchanged, or generated in connection with the due diligence process.
additional_definitions.Data Room: "Data Room" means any physical or virtual repository, platform, electronic storage environment, information-sharing portal, or secure information exchange mechanism used to provide access to Due Diligence Information.
additional_definitions.Evaluation Materials: "Evaluation Materials" means analyses, compilations, summaries, notes, reports, memoranda, financial models, valuation models, studies, presentations, and other materials prepared by or on behalf of a Party that contain, reflect, are based upon, or otherwise incorporate Due Diligence Information or Transaction Information.

confidential_information_expansion: (a) ownership information, shareholding information, capitalization tables, corporate structures, subsidiary information, and group organizational structures;
(b) audited financial statements, management accounts, budgets, forecasts, financial models, valuation reports, revenue analyses, profitability analyses, and financial projections;
(c) customer contracts, supplier contracts, distributor agreements, commercial arrangements, strategic partnerships, and material business relationships;
(d) material contracts, financing agreements, security documents, shareholder agreements, joint venture agreements, and transaction-related agreements;
(e) litigation records, dispute records, arbitration records, claims, notices, investigations, and contingent liabilities;
(f) tax records, tax filings, tax assessments, tax disputes, tax strategies, and tax compliance information;
(g) employment information, employee records, compensation structures, benefit plans, retention arrangements, and management information;
(h) intellectual property portfolios, patent registrations, trademark registrations, copyrights, trade secrets, know-how, technology assets, and licensing arrangements;
(i) regulatory filings, licenses, permits, approvals, compliance reports, audit reports, regulatory correspondence, and compliance assessments;
(j) valuation methodologies, pricing assumptions, transaction structures, deal models, negotiation strategies, transaction terms, and commercial positions;
(k) information contained within any virtual data room, management presentation, information memorandum, teaser, due diligence report, transaction report, or transaction document;
(l) acquisition plans, integration plans, restructuring plans, synergy analyses, post-closing strategies, and business transition plans; and

(m) any other commercial, financial, legal, tax, operational, strategic, technical, regulatory, compliance-related, transaction-related, or proprietary information disclosed in connection with the Transaction.

Service Provider Evaluation.purpose_definition: the evaluation, assessment, qualification, selection, engagement, onboarding, management, or potential appointment of a service provider, managed service provider, outsourcing provider, consultant, contractor, professional advisor, or other service organization by one or more of the Parties.
recitals: WHEREAS, the Parties desire to evaluate and discuss a potential service relationship, outsourcing arrangement, managed services engagement, professional services engagement, or other service-based commercial relationship;
